newShouldIssues.title: The claimed ambiguity-before-digest-match precedence is not pinned by any discriminating control
newShouldIssues.firstFailingBoundary: docs/coop/design-corrections/workflows/workflows_model.v1.py, verify_scope_parameter_binding, between the len(rows) > 1 guard (:713) and the payloadDigest match (:717)

counterexample.input: analysis spec selecting TWO ScopeDocumentV1 rows A and B, with a supplied document C that is NEITHER candidate

newShouldIssues.why: Both existing controls supply a document that IS one of the two candidate rows. For those inputs the guard-first and match-first orderings BOTH yield CONFIG.INVALID, so neither control discriminates the ordering it is named after. Moving the guard after the payload match left check-identity.py passing at 1592/0 against a passing unmutated control. The source argues the ordering is load-bearing at :689-696, and the native unit already meets this standard with cb8-unregistered-capability-outranks-the-ownership-tuple-rule.
newShouldIssues.scope: Control/test-evidence defect only. The SHIPPED ordering is CORRECT and the harm the prose names (obtaining a verified digest under an ambiguous spec) IS covered, because deleting the guard outright was detected.
newShouldIssues.remedy: Add one negative vector: ambiguous spec plus a non-candidate document, asserting CONFIG.INVALID rather than BASELINE.SCOPE_PARAMETER_DIGEST_MISMATCH.

newAdvisories.title: The canonical foundation exit code is machine-speed dependent, and a timeout leaves a stale passing report
newAdvisories.observed: check-identity.py measured 119.4s and 122.7s here; the declared elapsed for the whole foundation runner is 121.4s, itself at the boundary. On TimeoutExpired the wrapper raises before line 23, so validation-report.json retains its earlier passing content while the command exits 1.
newAdvisories.impact: A reader who checks the report rather than the exit code can see a passing report from a run that did not complete. The five sub-checks pass and regenerate byte-identical reports, so this is reproducibility hygiene, not a semantic defect.

newAdvisories.title: The 31-protected-file preservation claim is not verifiable within the declared review subject
newAdvisories.observed: 21 of the 31 protected paths are absent from the frozen subject (all docs/coop/architecture/*, several docs/v2/architecture/*, IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md, IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md). Within the subject only 10 are checkable.
newAdvisories.resolution: I verified all 31 against the read-only live source: 31 unchanged, 0 mismatched, 0 missing. The claim is TRUE; the note is that its evidence base extends beyond the subject.

newAdvisories.title: One ambiguity control asserts by source-text counting
newAdvisories.observed: 'the-scope-ambiguity-detail-is-a-code-this-model-already-published' asserts count("'CONFIG.INVALID', 'CONFIG.INVALID'")==1 and count("CONFIG.INVALID")>2 over the model's own source text. Strictly, CONFIG.INVALID is already published elsewhere as an error_code, and as a DETAIL only at this site.
newAdvisories.impact: Brittle under unrelated edits and slightly looser than its name. The substantive assertion — closed-registry and enum membership — is made separately and correctly at :1373-1375, so nothing rests on the text count alone.

CB-GAP-1.independentBasis: At-most-one is enforced per REGISTERED ROW and runs before the payload comparison; zero stays legal for ordinary analysis and is refused only for a requested binding; ambiguity uses the already-closed CONFIG.INVALID. Mutation controls: deleting the guard and making zero silently default were both DETECTED by check-identity.py against a passing unmutated control.
CB-GAP-1.residual: See NEW-SHOULD-1: the ordering itself is not pinned by a discriminating test.

CB-GAP-2.independentBasis: The ownership tuple is TYPED and never concatenated; the concatenating projection is explicitly superseded and nothing composes it. Prospective and retained boundaries call one helper. The precedence claim is backed by a vector carrying BOTH an unregistered capability and a tuple duplicate. Default construction emits the registered internal key before admit_analysis_spec (guard-first) while an explicit spec reaches schema uniqueItems first; the helper emits the key alone and the host supplies origin, so no origin is guessed.

CB-GAP-3.independentBasis: Independently recomputed the ladder: 17 registered (relation, rung) pairs, 12 non-resolved, 5 resolved. RC-6 is checked before the rung branch and WITHOUT `continue`, so it is total over all 17. It is an implication, not an equality: unknown+true and unknown+false remain legal. RC-0 short-circuits before RC-6 and its vector carries both faults; RC-6/RC-2 independence is shown by a vector expecting BOTH. No pre-existing vector was weakened: the three older coverage_bijection cases make no coverage=complete claim, and the other complete-injecting cases run sufficiency_v2, which by its own docstring knows nothing about resolution completeness.

CB-GAP-4.independentBasis: Both outputDomains sites are flat $ref '#/$defs/Domain' with identical uniqueItems/maxItems/vocabulary annotation, so existing walkers traverse them. Domain enum and byDomain agree exactly at 32 in both directions. Equality of the two arrays is stated separately from membership. The empty array declares no output and confers no authority. The operation token is provider-owned with shape-only admission and no platform-wide enum. Collision prose commits the COMPLETE stage spec including Plan and output domains, with cache keys committing that digest alongside their other declared inputs; no RunId-stability claim is made.

CB-GAP-5.independentBasis: Counted exactly 6 direct, 2 equalToDirect and 7 selectedThroughOtherInput members. The selection law states a required minimum, not an exact minimal set; extra admissible retained selections are legal and change PlanId; the standing explicitly excludes unreferenced CAS blobs from evaluation inputs.

CB-ADV-1.independentBasis: The registered-schema-document class is enforced at BOTH required sites, retention branches first, and the membership set is derived from the ONE payload registry (6 documents). Executed directly: empty, subset and registered-extra declarations are ADMITTED; arbitrary retained bytes refuse SCHEMA_DOCUMENT_UNREGISTERED; unretained bytes refuse BLOB_UNAVAILABLE first. The declaration remains a producer declaration and never a derived union.

CB-ADV-2.independentBasis: The exact evidence/Plan importIds equality (IMPORT_JOIN), the evaluated-subset rule (UNSELECTED_EVALUATION_IMPORT) and finding citability are three distinct joins at three sites; selection still requires retention/admission even when unused. No implicit imported facts.

CB-ADV-3.assessment: ACCOUNTED; correctly left as a bounded limitation.
CB-ADV-3.independentBasis: The disposition concedes that one shared lost blob may mask a second join and that finite tests do not establish only one dependency. That is the honest scope; I did not find it overstated.

CB-ADV-4.assessment: ACCOUNTED as a carried obligation, not closed.
CB-ADV-4.independentBasis: faultCause enum 12 versus inherited 11 is routed under the existing SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE host-invariant with inherited bytes preserved; reconciliation is explicitly deferred to application.

CX-V20-STAGE-REF-COMPATIBILITY.independentBasis: Both sites use the flat ref and are constraint-symmetric; the deep-ref variant root originally proposed is absent.

V20-ROOT-3.independentBasis: Both baseline-scope details are members of the closed registry AND the mirrored enum; the two sets agree exactly at 289 with zero drift in either direction. Removing either member from either side was DETECTED. Emissions, codes, remedies and reachability are unchanged; only admissibility changed. Refusals compose a schema-admitted failure envelope at exit 2, and an unregistered probe name still refuses on both shapes, so the carrier check is not vacuous.

V20-ROOT-4.independentBasis: See CB-GAP-2; the previously bespoke unregistered key is replaced by the registered ownership-tuple key with a public route.

V20-ROOT-5.assessment: ACCOUNTED, with the honest limit kept.
V20-ROOT-5.independentBasis: Remedies are keyed by public code, so a shared code's string must stay true for every internal key routing to it. The two widened strings do state BOTH conditions, so I judge them truthful as review evidence. Table equality is machine-checked; the English next-step semantics are not, and the record says so.

CX-V20-SENTINEL-SUCCESS.independentBasis: adopt_baseline's own duplicate-fingerprint guard raises Refusal(..., detail=None), so root's earlier `.detail is None` projection genuinely could not distinguish a refusal from a successful return. I regressed the positive to that form and it PASSED while asserting nothing about the binding, which demonstrates the supersession is substantive rather than cosmetic. The object() sentinel distinguishes ANY Refusal from a return.

CX-V20-FINAL-FIXTURE.independentBasis: The fixture declares f20b8353..., which is the afterSha256 of native-evidence.schemas.v2.json and NOT the earlier route digest 82745fa9..., so the refresh is real. Substituting the stale route digest was DETECTED by 'v20-native-view-fixture-declares-current-registered-schemas' against a passing control, so the drift guard is live. The view remains a bounded fragment and claims no sealed Run.

CX-V20-REVIEW-PRECISION.assessment: RESOLVED for the items I could check.
CX-V20-REVIEW-PRECISION.independentBasis: The collision prose no longer omits Plan/outputDomains; the RC-0 precedence vector now carries competing faults; historical evidence is preserved. The analogous workflow-scope precedence vector is still non-competing, which is NEW-SHOULD-1.
